diagram_candidates.exact_source_claim: For f(z)=z+μ̅z with |μ|<1, the unit circle maps to an ellipse with semiaxes 1+|μ| and 1−|μ|; finite round annuli map to rings between homothetic ellipses.
diagram_candidates.diagram_kind: complex-plane affine map and nested annulus map
diagram_candidates.reason: The principal-axis scaling and preservation of annular nesting are concrete geometric claims that a paired source/image sketch can check.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Show the unit circle and image ellipse, mark principal axes and the (1+|μ|),(1−|μ|) scale factors after the stated output rotation, then show two concentric circles mapping to homothetic ellipses bounding the image ring. Check axis orientation and ensure the puncture/infinity end cases are not misrepresented.
diagram_candidates.certainty: uncertain optional candidate; the formulas are explicit and the diagram is supplementary.

diagram_candidates.exact_source_claim: γ(t)=(1+t)exp(2πit), 0≤t≤1, starts at 1 and ends at 2 after one counterclockwise turn; its argument rises by 2π, while the path is not closed.
diagram_candidates.diagram_kind: oriented spiral path in the complex plane
diagram_candidates.reason: The distinction between one full turn and a closed contour is central to the example and easy to check visually.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Draw p=0, an outward spiral with arrow from γ(0)=1 to γ(1)=2, mark one complete angular turn, and distinguish the unequal endpoints. Do not label a winding number.
diagram_candidates.certainty: uncertain optional candidate; source parametrization determines the geometry.

diagram_candidates.exact_source_claim: The curve germ factors into two branches y=±x√(1+x), meeting only at the origin and with distinct tangent directions y=±x.
diagram_candidates.reason: The two branches and their distinct tangents explain the ordinary node geometry underlying the factorization.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Sketch both local branches through (0,0), mark tangent lines y=x and y=−x, and show the sole local intersection at the origin; use a small neighborhood and label the square-root factor as local.
diagram_candidates.certainty: uncertain optional candidate; illustrative only, with local branch behavior source-supported.

diagram_candidates.exact_source_claim: A line cuts the smooth cubic in Q1+Q2+Q3 with Q1⊕Q2⊕Q3=O; a secant/tangent gives P⊕Q=−R, vertical lines give P,−P,O, and the line at infinity cuts 3O.
diagram_candidates.reason: The chord/tangent law and the sign arising from reflection in the x-axis are geometric claims for which a carefully labeled sketch can catch sign errors.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Show a nonsingular real cubic as an illustrative affine curve, a nonvertical secant through P,Q with third intersection R, its reflected point −R, plus a tangent case and a vertical line through P,−P; label O at infinity and the line-at-infinity intersection 3O. Keep multiplicities explicit and state the sketch is illustrative.
diagram_candidates.certainty: uncertain optional candidate; the source claim is explicit, but a generic real sketch may not represent every complex cubic.

diagram_candidates.exact_source_claim: Each orbit has a representative τ with |Re τ|≤1/2 and |τ|≥1; applying T translates horizontally, while S sends τ to −1/τ and would increase imaginary part inside |τ|<1.
diagram_candidates.diagram_kind: upper-half-plane modular fundamental domain and orbit moves
diagram_candidates.reason: The standard domain is defined by two vertical boundaries and the unit-circle arc; these are tangible boundaries and transformations whose direction can be checked in a diagram.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Draw H, vertical lines Re τ=±1/2, unit-circle arc |τ|=1 between the boundary points, shade |Re τ|≤1/2 and |τ|≥1, and indicate T horizontal translation and S inversion across the unit circle. Avoid claiming uniqueness on identified boundary edges.
diagram_candidates.certainty: uncertain optional candidate; the orbit reduction is explicit, but a diagram only illustrates the reduction argument.
